doc.title: Ron Carter interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 17, 1999

title: Four and More: the Lincoln Center civil rights benefit
summary: Carter recalls Miles playing a benefit, his objection to playing unpaid, and that the band did not know it was recorded.

story.theme_name: Playing with and around Miles Davis
story.community_name: Playing with Miles Davis: joining, sessions and the band

blocks.x: Okay, just to wrap up here. I was looking at a book entitled 100 Best Jazz Albums, Len Lyons, you’re on at least five of them.
Maybe to make a quick comment about some of them mentioned.

That was done at Lincoln Center. People don’t realize that Miles was a real civil activist and he would often play for these civil rights fundraisers. And that night was a fundraiser for some civil rights group, I can’t remember, NAACP or something like that. We’d been off about four months, and he told us this is a benefit. So maybe I guess I was the spokesperson of the band said, it’s a benefit, okay, well why don’t you benefit them and let us have our money? And if I decide I want to benefit them I’ll give them a share of my salary. And he said he didn’t think so. So I said well I’ve got to go home man. And he says was I serious? I said yes. How do you benefit with our money? And he said okay. And we got paid, then whatever happened happened. But none of us knew it was being
recorded. We didn’t know it was recorded until a year after the record was out, so that was a whole other process, a whole other thing on the scene. And that’s one of the stories behind that record.
